label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all fall in the higher range compared to other profiles, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring psychological distress alongside heavy digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness as indicated by a UCLA-8 mean of approximately 1.78
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology with a PHQ-9 mean of approximately 1.81
Notably high anxiety symptoms with a GAD-7 mean of approximately 2.27, the most pronounced distress indicator in this profile
Pattern of co-occurring emotional difficulties alongside intensive digital media engagement
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of psychological distress and heavy social-media involvement observed in this group

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report lower loneliness, lower depressive symptoms, and lower anxiety compared to other groups. They engage in relatively light daily social-media use, averaging roughly 2.8 hours per day (within the 1–3 hour bracket). Their psychological well-being indicators are consistently favorable, with notably low scores on loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78), depression (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27), and anxiety (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03).
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use approximately 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media consumption averaging around 2.8 hours
Consistently low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Moderate and bounded engagement with social media rather than heavy or excessive use
tone: Stable, psychologically resilient, and measured in digital engagement

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness yet comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms, while spending nearly five hours per day on social media. Their loneliness scores sit above the sample norm, suggesting persistent feelings of social disconnection, but these do not translate into proportionally high clinical mood or anxiety indicators. Their heavy daily social-media engagement may serve as a compensatory social outlet or may itself contribute to their sense of isolation.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) relative to other profiles
Below-average depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Below-average anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Heavy daily social-media use averaging close to 5 hours (midpoint ≈ 4.89 hours)
Disconnect between subjective loneliness and clinical distress levels
tone: Socially disconnected yet psychologically resilient; quietly seeking connection through digital channels

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents a relatively large group (n = 217) of male respondents with graduate-level education who report low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social-media use is light, averaging roughly 1.6 hours per day (self-reported range of 1–3 hours). Across all three psychological well-being scales, their scores fall well below clinical concern thresholds, suggesting generally positive mental health and social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.22), indicating strong perceived social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82), well below clinical screening thresholds
Low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.90), suggesting generally calm and regulated affect
Engagement with social media that does not appear to displace offline social or professional activities
tone: Calm, balanced, and socially secure — reflecting a respondent group that appears psychologically well-adjusted with disciplined, moderate digital habits
